Battletech.

I know there is renewed development of the source material already, but Battletech has one giant problem:

The coolest setting in its timeline is 3025 where mechs are exceedingly rare artifacts of ancient power, owning even just the smallest one of them enables you to rule a whole planet, and a 100 ton mech is like a fabled monster that takes to the field from the nightmares of anyone who doesn't have one.

The coolest mechs however aren't all around until the 3067+ years, where mechs are mass produced and piloted by commoners that were recruited to the army. No mech is truly rare and outstanding during that timeframe, even clan tech has somewhat lost it's edge, and inner sphere tech is a confusing jumble of prototype and novelty parts with not a single genuine improvement made to any common item.

That schism between the most interesting setting and the most interesting mechs is fucking over battletech, because people want their Madcats and Fafnirs and Atlas-Ks, and Gauss Rifles and ER PPCs and double heatsinks and Ultra AC 20s, but in order to have those you have to play during a time when mechs have already become mundane, most of the interesting characters are long dead, and the setting is just slowly winding down to orbital nuclear war.

On top of that the fact that you aren't canonically allowed to simply invent a new mech for a story set in 3025 absolutely sucks. New mechs are fun, dreaming them up, flipping through the tech manuals, finding the one you think just looks the most awesome out of all of them is a huge part of it, but to long time fans that magic is gone because all anyone can ever do is re-imagine existing models.

So from my perspective in order for Battletech to truly be revitalized they need to do a hard reboot, and consolidate the things people like from all the advancement with the things the franchise has lost and the ability to introduce new ideas without having to keep advancing the story.
